repo_notes.content: demo-ledger-service is a shared library, not a deployable service. It is consumed as a pinned Git-tag dependency by eventflow-order-service (ledger.settlement) and eventflow-payment-service (ledger.fees / ledger.invoice) in the same GitHub organisation. The README 'Accounting conventions' section is authoritative when code and documentation disagree.

pages.title: Overview
pages.purpose: What demo-ledger-service is: a pure-Python fund ledger library (settlement dates, fees, invoices, day counts, positions, realised P&L) with no I/O or framework, published as an installable package from a Git tag. Summarise the module table from the README and the accounting conventions that govern behaviour.

pages.title: Installing and Releasing
pages.purpose: How the package is built (PEP 517, setuptools, the `ledger` package), how consumers install it from a pinned Git tag (pip and Poetry examples), and the release procedure: bump `version` in pyproject.toml and `ledger.__version__`, merge, then tag `vX.Y.Z`. Explain why the tag, not a registry, is the dependency mechanism.

pages.title: Modules
pages.purpose: One section per module under ledger/: models, markets, settlement, fees, invoice, daycount, positions, pnl. For each, list the public functions/classes, their inputs and outputs, and the accounting rule from the README they implement (T+N business days, round-half-up money, 30/360 US rule, FIFO lot relief).

pages.title: Consumers
pages.purpose: The 'Case 3' shared-library topology: which sibling repositories depend on this library, which module each one uses (order-service computes expected settlement dates via ledger.settlement.settlement_date; payment-service computes a processing-fee line via ledger.fees.management_fee), how they pin the tag in pyproject.toml, and what a consumer must do when a new tag is released.

pages.title: Testing and CI
pages.purpose: The pytest suite layout (one test file per module, invoice fixtures in tests/fixtures/invoices.json), how to run it locally, and what .github/workflows/ci.yml runs on push and pull request.
